concept.name: Schema validation
concept.definition: The automated checking of a data instance (e.g., a JSON document) against a formal schema that declares its required structure, types, and constraints, using a validator implementing the schema specification. In the JSON ecosystem, a JSON Schema validator verifies that a document conforms to the declared keywords before the data is accepted.
concept.intuition: A bouncer with a checklist: data gets in only if every required field is present, correctly typed, and within the declared limits.
concept.mechanics: A schema defines properties, types, required fields, ranges, patterns, and allowed enumerations; the validator walks the instance and reports every keyword violation. Validation is run at ingestion boundaries — on model outputs, API payloads, and knowledge-base entries — to reject malformed data before it propagates.
concept.failure_modes: Validation enforces only what the schema declares: underspecified schemas admit garbage, and no schema can check factual accuracy or semantic appropriateness. Version drift between producers and validators (different schema drafts) causes false accepts and rejects.
concept.misconceptions: Passing validation does not mean the data is good — only that it is well-formed. Schema validation is also not a substitute for domain-level checks such as cross-field consistency or source verification.
concept.example: Every entry in this library is validated against the entry schema — required fields like id, definition, status, and citations — so a missing citation array fails the build rather than silently degrading the knowledge base.
